sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mabon was a Welsh hero and a divine youth. He appears in the early Arthurian tale Kulhwch and Olwen as Mabon vab Modron, which means Son, Son of Mother. No father is mentioned. Another figure of the same name is called Mabon vab Mellt, from the patronym of his father MeLLts. An early text calls Mabon one of the Three Exalted Captives of the Island of Britain. In the Mabinogion, Kulhwch rescues Mabon from the Otherworld, where he was held after being stolen from his mother in infancy. So many years passed that Mabon was the oldest living human. After his rescue he helped Kulhwch win the hand of Olwen. Two similar figures, Mabonagrain and Mabunz, also appear as captives in Arthurian literature. Some derive the name of the Mabinogion from Mabon. Others connect him with the obscure god Maponus.

okr.objective: Document Mabon as a Welsh hero and divine youth linked to the god Maponus.
